text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices climbed on escalating geopolitical tensions in key energy-producing regions. Ukraine intensified drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure over the weekend, while Iran signaled readiness to respond to potential U.S. attacks and has been escalating strikes in the Strait of Hormuz — a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. These developments pushed Brent crude near $109-$110 a barrel, supporting prices for major oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

The stock's broader two-week rally of 15.6% reflects a sustained tightening in oil markets beyond just today's headlines. Tanker rates have surged significantly, adding roughly $38 per barrel to the cost of physically delivering oil, which means the effective price pressure on global energy supplies is even more acute than the headline crude price suggests — a dynamic that benefits integrated producers with refining operations.
